For every type E equipped with exactly the ambient structures
  NormedAddCommGroup E, InnerProductSpace R E, FiniteDimensional R E,
  MeasurableSpace E, BorelSpace E,
let volume be its actual finite-dimensional real Hilbert Lebesgue/Haar measure. There is no separate CompleteSpace E or Nontrivial E binder; zero-dimensional E is allowed. Let F:E->R be an arbitrary function, p:E an arbitrary point, and s:R an arbitrary real scalar satisfying s!=0.
Define the genuine affine map phi(x)=p+s scalar-multiplied x, whose inverse is psi(x)=s^(-1) scalar-multiplied (x-p). Then the exact measure equality is
  Measure.map(phi)(volume.tilted(x -> -F(x)))
    = volume.tilted(x -> -F(psi(x))).
For every measure nu, the supplied definition is
  nu.tilted(h)=nu.withDensity(x -> ENNReal.ofReal(exp(h(x))/integral exp(h) dnu)).
The real Bochner integral normalization is totalized outside exponential integrability; a zero denominator gives zero density by real division by zero. The statement has no measurability, continuity, C2, exponential-integrability, positive-normalizer, curvature or moment premise on F. The only explicit nonstructural premise is s!=0, allowing both positive and negative scales. There is no probability premise on either measure and no probability conclusion. In particular the equality of these actual possibly totalized measures must not be promoted into a claim that the measures are probability laws.
The right-hand side is exactly the normalized tilt by -F composed with the inverse affine map, with no residual scalar Jacobian multiplier displayed. Dimension zero remains in scope, with no dimension-positive hypothesis. No parameter space, measurable selector, posterior family, kernel, gradient, second moment, covariance, score estimate or algorithm conclusion appears. The newly approved ambient context supplies the exact missing instance list, so there is no remaining definition or ambient-binder ambiguity. No CompleteSpace premise or hypotheses of another declaration are inserted.

after.text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, CompleteSpace, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances. Its volume is the actual full-space real Hilbert Lebesgue/Haar measure; dimension zero is allowed. Let S be an arbitrary measurable space. Let V:E->R and kappa:R satisfy kappa>=1, V is twice continuously Frechet differentiable, and for every x,v in E BOTH
  kappa^(-1)*||v||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x v) v,
  (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x v) v <= ||v||^2.
Let eta:S->R and y:S->E be measurable, with 0<eta(s)<=1 for every s in S. The gradient is the genuine real Hilbert Riesz representative of the Frechet derivative.
There exists ONE map p:S->E such that p is measurable and for every s in S,
  p(s)+eta(s) scalar-multiplied gradient V(p(s))=y(s).
For that same p define the following literal objects:
  rho(s,u)=V(p(s)+sqrt(eta(s)) scalar-multiplied u)-V(p(s))
           -sqrt(eta(s))*inner R (gradient V(p(s))) u,
  Q(s,u)=||u||^2/2+rho(s,u),
  mu=volume.tilted(x -> -V(x)),
  R(s)=mu.tilted(x -> -||x-y(s)||^2/(2*eta(s))),
  r(s)=Measure.map(x -> (sqrt(eta(s)))^(-1) scalar-multiplied (x-p(s)))(R(s)).
Then mu is a probability measure, and for EVERY s in S ALL the following hold simultaneously:
(1) R(s) is a probability measure.
(2) rho(s,-) is C2 and Q(s,-) is C2.
(3) gradient(rho(s,-))(0)=0 and gradient(Q(s,-))(0)=0.
(4) For every u,v in E,
  0 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R (rho(s,-))) u v) v <= eta(s)*||v||^2.
(5) For every u,v in E,
  ||v||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R (Q(s,-))) u v) v <= (1+eta(s))*||v||^2.
(6) The exact standardized law identity is
  r(s)=volume.tilted(u -> -Q(s,u)).
(7) r(s) is a probability measure, and MemLp id 2 (r(s)) holds, meaning true AE strong measurability and a finite vector L2 norm for the position function.
(8) u -> ||u||^2 is integrable with respect to r(s), and
  integral ||u||^2 dr(s)(u) <= Module.finrank R E.
(9) MemLp (gradient(rho(s,-))) 2 (r(s)) holds, meaning a genuine vector L2 gradient.
(10) BOTH exact real gradient-energy bounds hold:
  integral ||gradient(rho(s,-))(u)||^2 dr(s)(u)
    <= (eta(s))^2 * integral ||u||^2 dr(s)(u),
  integral ||gradient(rho(s,-))(u)||^2 dr(s)(u)
    <= (eta(s))^2 * Module.finrank R E.
Each C2, zero-gradient and lower/upper-Hessian conjunct above is separate and retained. The two last inequalities are uncentered squared-norm integrals, with no energy factor1/2 and no substituted mean or covariance. Their measure is the SAME actual standardized r(s), not the original volume, mu, or R(s).
Every tilt is the actual normalized exponential withDensity construction. The theorem separately PRODUCES probability for mu,R(s),r(s), real vector L2 and norm-square integrability, so the law and moment claims are not inferred solely from a totalized measure equality or an outside-integrability fallback. No positive partition, posterior moment, score bound, or selector certificate is supplied as a hypothesis. The affine normalization is represented by the exact equality to volume.tilted(-Q); no uncancelled Jacobian factor is asserted. The scope is every positive step size at most1, including1, and the whole E including dimension zero; kappa only has the displayed real lower bound1.
The existential p precedes every let-defined rho,Q,mu,R,r and all their conjuncts. The probability of mu is outside the subsequent forall s and is not made vacuous if S is empty. No joint measurability of s->R(s) or s->r(s), Markov posterior kernel, measurable disintegration, uniform-in-parameter integral, unequal-step comparison, Gaussian gradient-output law, HMC transition, bias/MGF, query count, transport, algorithm or whole-paper conclusion is stated. The only selector conclusion is its measurability and the exact first-order equation; no extra minimizer/growth/uniqueness clause is inserted.
